subject_mention: image digest drift + webhook CA skew
evidence_span: Confirmed two simultaneous failure modes: image digest drift + webhook CA skew. Either alone might be recoverable; together they blocked automated in-place remediation in customer clusters.

nodeagent image referenced by the release manifest was removed from the upstream registry and a new digest was pushed under the same tag between CI artifact publish and chart rendering, causing ImagePullBackOff/crashloop.

the mutating/validating webhook CA bundle in the Helm chart was rotated independently by our release automation resulting in webhook TLS verification failures (conversion/mutation requests rejected) for existing kube objects.

a low-priority thread (per-NUMA) scans segments flagged as fragmented and performs compaction by moving live entries into newly allocated pages in the same pool and freeing fully-empty pages.

object_mention: pools grow/shrink in unit segment increments
evidence_span: Pools grow/shrink in unit segment increments to keep fragmentation within a target window.
Pick victim pool according to pool pressure (weighted by allocation failure + tail latency budget).
A segment is a contiguous region composed of fixed-size pages (e.g., 4KB host pinned, 8KB GPU) which are the minimum allocation unit visible to the allocator.
extremely small KV entries (e.g., <64B) are placed into an overlay slab within a page to avoid wasting page-level metadata for many tiny items.
Segment header (compact): pool-id, segment-id (32-bit), total-pages (16-bit), free-pages (16-bit), flags (fragmented, compacting, pinned), generation-clock (8-bit), epoch.
Page metadata (per-page small struct): page-offset, freelist-head, occupancy-bitmap (for slab pages), approximate-hotness-score (8-bit), last-touch-ts (monotonic counter small).
Entry format: entry-id, key-hash (64-bit), size-in-pages (8-bit), generation (2-3 bits), pointer(s)/offsets.
